sentences.text: Torosteus resembled Incisoscutum and Compagopiscis in body size and shape, suggesting it may have lived a pelagic lifestyle.
The large number of Torosteus fossils found suggests the possibility of schooling behavior.
Fossils of Torosteus have been found in the Kimberley region of Australia.
Analysis of bite force suggests that Torosteus was an active predator.
Torosteus is currently classified as a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea within the clade Coccosteomorphi.
Torosteus was an extinct arthrodire placoderm that lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Torosteus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
